# wallix-bastion_profile (Data Source)

Get information on a profile resource, including its GUI permission levels, dashboards, and any
target/user group scope limitations.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get information about a specific profile
data "wallix-bastion_profile" "administrator" {
  profile_name = "administrator"
}

# Assign the looked-up profile to a user
resource "wallix-bastion_user" "admin_user" {
  user_name  = "admin.user"
  email      = "admin@company.com"
  profile    = data.wallix-bastion_profile.administrator.profile_name
  user_auths = ["local_password"]
}

# Inspect whether the profile can manage target groups
output "can_modify_target_groups" {
  value = data.wallix-bastion_profile.administrator.gui_features[0].target_groups == "modify"
}
```

## Usage Notes

### `profile_name`

The Required lookup key. It must match an existing profile exactly; the data source fails with an
error if no profile with that name exists.

### `gui_features` and `gui_transmission`

Both are single-element lists (blocks) exposing one string attribute per manageable area
(`wab_audit`, `system_audit`, `users`, `user_groups`, `devices`, `target_groups`,
`authorizations`, `profiles`, `wab_settings`, `system_settings`, `backup`, `approval`,
`credential_recovery` — `gui_transmission` has all of these except `wab_audit`). Each attribute
reports the permission level currently granted for that area:

- **view**: Read-only access
- **modify**: Read and write access
- **execute**: Permission to execute actions (e.g. `backup`, `credential_recovery`)
- An empty string means no access is granted for that area

`gui_features` controls access to Bastion management features, while `gui_transmission` controls
access during session transmission/monitoring.

### `target_access` / `ip_limitation` / `dashboards`

- **target_access**: Whether the profile is allowed to access targets at all
- **ip_limitation**: The IP address/subnet restriction applied to the profile, if any
- **dashboards**: The set of dashboards available to the profile

### `target_groups_limitation` / `user_groups_limitation`

Both are lists that are empty (zero elements) when the corresponding limitation is not enabled on
the profile, and contain exactly one block when it is:

- **target_groups_limitation**: `default_target_group` (the default target group applied) and
  `target_groups` (the set of target groups the profile is restricted to)
- **user_groups_limitation**: `user_groups` (the set of user groups the profile is restricted to
  manage)

Always check `length(...)` on these lists before indexing into them, since they can legitimately
be empty.
